      <description>120 avviste asylsøkere i Danmark oppfyller kriteriene for å bli sendt til et retursenter i Rwanda neste år.
Det opplyser det danske utlendings- og integreringsdepartementet til DR.
Det er bare asylsøkere som ikke har barn eller er blitt dømt til kriminalitet som kan bli sendt til Rwanda, ifølge allmennkringkasteren. Dette skal gjelde 120 av 365 avviste asylsøkere.

      <description>Timon Haugan leverte med presset som leder etter første omgang og kjørte inn til seier på slalåmen i Gurgl. Han ble med det første nordmann med verdenscupseier i Gurgl.
24 år gamle Eirik Hystad Solberg overrasket stort på og ble nummer to - hans første pallplass på toppnivå.
Atle Lie McGrath var nummer to før finaleomgangen, men hektet i en port og forsvant ut. I frustrasjon kastet han stavene og ble liggende ved siden av løypa. Også Henrik Kristoffersen, som var nummer seks etter første omgang, kjørte ut i finalen.
Lucas Pinheiro Braathen jaktet sin tredje strake seier - men 26-åringen kjørte ut i første omgang.</description>

      <title>Karoline Grøtting best av alle på sesongåpningens siste dag – skiskytter imponerte</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/karoline-grotting-best-av-alle-pa-sesongapningens-siste-dag-_-skiskytter-imponerte-1.18086614</link>
      <description>Karoline Grøtting var best av samtlige kvinner under dagens 15 kilometer fristil på Beitostølen.
5 kilometer før mål sto kampen om seieren mellom Grøtting og Kristin Austgulen Fosnæs. Der var det altså Grøtting som til slutt trakk det lengste strået.
Grøtting stod over fredagens 10 kilometer på grunn av magesmerter i et forsøk på å spare seg til dagens distanse.
– Jeg er veldig glad for det nå, sier Grøtting til NRK etter målgang.
Skiskytter Ida Lien var dagens andre startende og gikk i mål til ledelse. Der ble hun værende til Grøtting overtok lederstolen.
Likevel holdt det til 3. plass for skiskytteren.
Heidi Weng vant fredagens 10 kilometer klassisk, men klarte ikke å gjenskape prestasjonen i dag. Allerede ved 6,2 kilometer hadde Weng 17 sekunder opp til teten.
Weng endte på 5. plass, 36 sekunder bak vinner.
Herrene skal ut på sin 15 kilometer klokken 13:00. Den kan du følge på NRK TV.</description>

      <title>Selvik reddet straffe på overtid da Brest vant igjen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/selvik-reddet-straffe-pa-overtid-da-brest-vant-igjen-1.18086449</link>
      <description>Egil Selvik fortsetter å storspille i Brest-målet. Lørdag sikret han 1-0-seier borte mot Strasbourg ved å redde straffespark fem minutter på overtid.
Sraffen ble dømt etter en VAR-gjennomgang av en situasjon der ballen traff armen til Brest-spiller Mama Baldé, men det berget ikke hjemmelaget.
Brest tok ledelsen ved Noah Edjouma i det 22. minutt, etter en svak klarering av keeper Filip Jørgensen. Selvik forsvarte ledelsen med en rekke gode redninger og hjalp laget sitt til den tredje strake seieren i Ligue 1.
Selvik voktet Norges mål i nasjonsligaseieren over Wales for en uke siden, men han måtte overraskende sette seg på benken igjen da Norge knep gruppeseieren med 3-2-seier over Danmark i Parken tirsdag. Da var Ørjan Nyland tilbake i målet. Lørdag satt Nyland på benken for RB Leipzig.
Brest-seieren løftet laget til 6.-plass på tabellen. Strasbourg har bare tre lag bak seg på tabellen.
(©NTB)</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/norwegian-ber-5000-kundar-sperre-bankkortet-etter-datainnbrot-1.18085456</link>
      <description>Norwegian har teke kontakt med rundt 5000 kundar og bede dei sperre bankkorta sine etter at ein leverandør til nettsidene deira er utsett for datainnbrot, melder NTB.
Ein skadeleg kode blei lagt inn på nettsidene til Norwegian, som gjorde at kortdetaljar som blei brukt på nettsida kan ha vore synlege i ein kortare periode måndag.
Selskapet oppdaga datainnbrotet onsdag.
Hendinga er rapportert til Datatilsynet.
I førre veke blei det kjent at 144.000 passasjerar hos Norwegian og Widerøe blei lekka i forbindelse med eit datainnbrot hos ein spansk IT-leverandør.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Israel med ny offensiv – tre drept</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/israel-med-ny-offensiv-_-tre-drept-1.18084431</link>
      <description>Israels hær sier den har innledet en operasjon i Hamas-kontrollerte områder i Gaza
Israel har innledet en militæroperasjon i det sentrale Gaza vest for den såkalte gule linjen, som har skilt Hamas-kontrollerte og israelsk-kontrollerte områder siden våpenhvilen trådte i kraft i fjor. Det opplyser militæret til AFP.
Vitner sier at israelske stridsvogner rullet inn på hovedveien Salahudeen, vest for den såkalte gule linjen som markerer grensen for de to tredjedelene av Gazastripen som fortsatt er under israelsk kontroll.
Den såkalte gule linjen ble etablert etter våpenhvilen i oktober 2025 og skiller israelskkontrollerte og palestinske soner i Gazastripen. Israelske styrker har gradvis flyttet den gule linjen og utvidet området under direkte militær kontroll i Gaza.</description>

IGV Housing says it can build a home for 30 per cent less than traditional building and it can get people into a home without a down payment.

The post IGV Housing in Port Alberni launches new path to home ownership appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

If you want to be a home owner but don’t have the down payment for one a company called IGV Housing in Port Alberni may have a plan for you.

The company has an advanced manufacturing facility in Port Alberni and it launched IGV Hope this week.

The company says it has a plan that could see people move into their home before having a down payment or needing a traditional mortgage at the outset.

Watch the report below:

Loading the player...

A celebratory ribbon cutting in Port Alberni marked the launch in front of more than 100 people Thursday.

The head of IGV Housing says a rethink on how traditional home building is done has long been needed.

“That’s what we’ve done. We’re taking the best from a number of different technologies, sewing them together, in what we call a hybrid construction methodology to actually deliver high quality housing more affordably,” said Josh Hunt, IGV’s Housing CEO and Founder.

Hunt says with less waste, in an automated protected environment it can build a home for 30 per cent less cost, and build it faster providing more certainty to buyers.

The company has fully renovated the former San Group sawmill and has 60 full-time employees ready to build homes largely inside.

“This manufacturing facility with two lines going, two shifts, can deliver 10,000 homes a year and so that obviously that could be absorbed just on Vancouver Island the demand is so huge but what we’re setting up is a duplicatable process that you could duplicate across Canada,” said Hunt.

It also has a plan for expediting building permits with pre-approved designs and for people to get into homes without a down payment.

That process would see a IGV home bought for a price that stays fixed for 10 years. The buyer can move in right away and make a monthly payment which, after 10 years, will be transitioned to a mortgage.

The idea is the buyer will be in a better financial position to get a mortgage after the 10 years because the owner has built equity and the home has likely increased in value.

“For working households and essential workers it means being able to live in the communities they’re actually contributing to,” said Sabrina Zacharias, the Program Manager of IGV Hope.

During the 10-year period, the property is held by a not-for-profit housing association.

Port Alberni’s Mayor says it’s amazing the company has come to Port Alberni with such an innovative plan.

“A different idea, especially with the financing to go with IGV Hope,” said Charles Mealey, Port Alberni Mayor. “I think it’s a really great opportunity for people that want to get into home ownership that might look at it right now and say they can’t, and this is an opportunity so they can.”

The region’s MLA it’s fantastic see a holistic approach to make home ownership more accessible

“I’m just so thrilled that they’ve chosen Port Alberni to be their home for what’s a really innovative manufacturing process and that they’re looking at more than just how to build a new home but how to help people to get into that new home,” said Josie Osborne, the MLA for Mid Island-Pacific Rim.

The company says its first phase of full production is scheduled to start in January, ramping up throughout the year.

It says it also has planning permits in Port Alberni, Ucluelet and Campbell River to deliver multiplex homes.

For those interested in exploring the model to get into a home, the company’s website is here.

A week-long hearing on whether a Powell River energy company can sell power to the U.S. has wrapped up, and it has met unilateral opposition.

The decision on whether or not Powell River Energy Inc. (PREI) can be granted a 30-year licence to export power to the U.S. is in the hands of the Canada Energy Regulator.

In 2025, the energy producer filed an unprecedented application, citing that it needed to secure financing to update its facilities.

Watch the report below:

Loading the player...

“This is a unique finite resource that belongs first and foremost to the people of this country,” said North Island–Powell River MP Aaron Gunn.

Gunn was among the several dozen residents in Powell River who oppose the potential approval, along Powell River City officials, Tla’amin First Nation members, advocates, and NDP MLA Randene Neill.

“I haven’t heard from a single resident in Powell River who supports this,” said Neill, the MLA for Powell River–Sunshine Coast.

The application for the license was launched in 2025 but the company has already been selling energy to the U.S. since 2021, after the nearby Catalyst Paper Mill shut down, costing the city more than 200 jobs.

PREI operates two dams, one at Powell Lake and the other at Lois Lake, and previously provided power to the mill.

Since the closure, the Tla’amin First Nation and Cranberry Business Group have taken over ownership. The Nation is arguing against the approval of the license, saying that it needs power to remain in the local community to reopen the mill, attract new tenants and recover the lost jobs from the mill’s closure.

“They’re asking for this unprecedented 30-year export permit at a time when we’re engaged in a trade war where they’veput unjustified and malicious tariffs against the very same industries that these dams used to support,” said Gunn.

However, PREI argued last week that it already contributes $10 million locally every year.

A lawyer for the energy producer said during talks on Friday that they attempted to seek a deal with B.C. Hydro for two years. However, PREI claims the provincial Crown corporation did not offer a competitive price and terms and conditions

Public hearing on consideration for the license ended on Friday. The Canada Energy Regulator (CRE) will now take at least 12 weeks to consider the application and provide a recommendation.

Ultimately, it will be up to federal cabinet members to make the final call if PREI can export to the U.S.

]]> 1363252 ‘We are looking for answers’: Family identifies woman who died at Port Hardy hospital https://cheknews.ca/we-are-looking-for-answers-family-identifies-woman-who-died-at-port-hardy-hospital-1363247/ Mon, 23 Nov 2026 00:08:22 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1363247

Courtney McCowan died Thursday night after being treated by paramedics outside Port Hardy Hospital, where the ER had closed for the night just minutes earlier.

The post ‘We are looking for answers’: Family identifies woman who died at Port Hardy hospital appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The family of Courtney McCowan is grieving the loss of a beloved mother, sister and friend — and wondering whether she would still be alive if things had gone differently.

McCowan, 48, died Thursday night after being treated by paramedics outside Port Hardy Hospital, where the emergency department had closed for the night just minutes earlier.

“As a family, we are struggling to process an unimaginable loss. We have lost an amazing mother, a sister, and a friend, and our hearts are broken. Alongside our grief, we are left with so many unanswered questions,” McCowan’s daughter Hailey Schubert told CHEK News Sunday.

Watch the report below:

Loading the player...

“We can’t stop wondering what happened, whether proper protocols were followed, and whether the systems in place were enough to protect her. We find ourselves asking whether she would still be here today if things had been done differently.”

McCowan’s family has now publicly identified her, two days after the circumstances surrounding her death were first reported.

Her brother, Frank McCowan, told CHEK News he rushed to Port Hardy Hospital after learning his sister had been taken there Thursday evening.

When he arrived, he saw two ambulances outside the hospital and emergency responders working to save her.

“I went inside, tried to talk to her, but…I already knew that she was gone,” he said.

Frank says he has been told his sister spent around 39 minutes receiving treatment outside the hospital before being brought inside, a timeline that has not been independently confirmed.

“Why was she left on the concrete for 39 minutes outside the hospital, dedicated to saving people’s lives?” he asked. “When there’s two doctors inside, I see no reason why she couldn’t have been brought in right away.”

According to BC Emergency Health Services, a paramedic at Port Hardy Hospital became aware of a patient requiring medical attention in the parking lot at 5:11 p.m. Thursday, 11 minutes past the 5 p.m. to 7 a.m. emergency room closure that has occurred nightly since 2023.

Two additional ambulances responded, and paramedics provided emergency treatment before transferring McCowan to hospital staff in critical condition.

She was subsequently pronounced dead.

Frank says he understands his sister may have been experiencing cardiac arrest when she was brought to the hospital, but doesn’t know the full circumstances of her medical emergency.

He praised the paramedics who attempted to save her life and despite his frustration, Frank says the family is not ready to assign blame without knowing exactly what happened.

“We don’t know all the facts, so it’s hard to point fingers,” he said.

McCowan had lived in Port Hardy for approximately 13 years and leaves behind a daughter and several siblings.

Island Health reviewing incident it calls ‘tragedy’

In a statement provided to CHEK News on Sunday, Island Health says it’s working with BCEHS to establish the circumstances surrounding McCowan’s death.

“Island Health clinical leadership remains in contact with BC Emergency Health Services leadership as we work to establish and clarify the facts of what occurred. All potential factors will be examined and considered,” the health authority said.

Island Health confirmed that ER-trained physicians and nurses were among the care teams that responded to the incident.

It also says immediate steps have been taken to reinforce existing procedures for patients who arrive at Port Hardy Hospital shortly after the emergency department closes.

“We are supporting staff and care providers with an incident debrief and any necessary follow up,” Island Health said.

The health authority did not provide a detailed timeline explaining when hospital staff became aware of McCowan’s condition or why she was initially treated outside.

“Our thoughts continue to be with the family members and loved ones affected by this tragedy,” Island Health said.

“We know it has affected many people in Port Hardy, including the Island Health care providers and first responders who delivered emergency medical treatment, and we are taking the situation extremely seriously.”

The BC Coroners Service is also investigating McCowan’s death.

Renewed calls for 24-hour emergency care

The death has renewed concerns about the ongoing overnight closure of Port Hardy Hospital’s emergency department.

Since 2023, the ER has closed nightly from 5 p.m. to 7 a.m., leaving residents without local overnight emergency department access.

Fran Jenkins has been calling for better health care in Port Hardy for years and held a rally back in 2023 to call attention to the issue.

She told CHEK News Sunday that a close friend of hers died this year while being transported to the nearest ER in Port McNeill because Port Hardy’s was closed. 

“We have a hospital, we have an emergency room and it should be open 24 hours a day,” she said.

Dr. Alex Nataros, a family physician with the North Island Community Health Centre, has been outspoken about the closures and believes the lack of overnight emergency services is putting patients at risk.

Local physicians have proposed designating Port Hardy Hospital as a permanent overnight emergency department for the North Island, arguing it would provide a more sustainable approach to emergency coverage in the region.

In its latest statement, Island Health acknowledged the proposal and said it remains committed to improving access.

Vancouver Islanders will have several opportunities to spot the International Space Station streaking across the evening sky over the next week, with some particularly bright passes expected.

According to NASA’s Spot the Station website, the orbiting laboratory will be visible from several Vancouver Island communities, including Victoria, Sidney, Nanaimo, Courtenay, Port Alberni and Gold River, through early December.

The ISS orbits Earth at an altitude of approximately 400 kilometres, travelling at a speed of roughly 28,000 kilometres per hour.

Despite that distance, the station is bright enough to be seen with the naked eye, even in urban areas with significant light pollution.

It typically appears as a bright white dot moving steadily across the sky, resembling an airplane without flashing lights.

Unlike an aircraft, however, the ISS moves much faster and does not change direction as it crosses the sky.

There will be several upcoming viewing opportunities for Island communities, with passes lasting between two and seven minutes.

Some of the best opportunities are expected later this week, when the station will climb particularly high above the horizon.

For Victoria, the best viewing times are below:

Friday, Nov. 27, could offer one of the best opportunities, with the ISS expected to be visible for seven minutes and reach a maximum height of 84 degrees — almost directly overhead.

During that pass, the station is expected to first appear 10 degrees above the west-northwestern horizon before travelling across the sky and disappearing toward the east-southeast.

NASA says the best time to see the ISS is shortly before sunrise or after sunset, when sunlight reflects off the station while the sky below is dark. No telescope or binoculars are required.

The station usually appears as one of the brightest objects in the night sky after the Moon, making it relatively easy to identify when conditions are clear.

The ISS completes an orbit around Earth approximately every 90 minutes, allowing astronauts aboard to experience 16 sunrises and sunsets each day.

The station has been continuously occupied since November 2000 and serves as an orbiting laboratory for scientific research involving international partners, including Canada.

Vancouver Islanders can also check upcoming viewing opportunities for their community through NASA’s Spot the Station website.
